title: The Search Begins
content:
The moment the network returned, Sneha immediately called her friend again.

"Tell me the rest," she said anxiously.

Her friend repeated the registered phone number, and after thanking him, Sneha wasted no time dialling it.

The call rang.

Once.

Twice.

Three times.

No answer.

She frowned and tried again.

The ringtone echoed through the silence before the call disconnected once more.

"Come on..." she muttered under her breath.

Determined not to give up, she dialed the number one final time. This time she waited patiently until the last ring faded away.

Still...

No one answered.

Frustrated, she threw herself back against the seat and let out a deep sigh.

Her thoughts drifted back to Siddu and the unfinished story he had left behind.

Suddenly, an idea struck her.

"Yagnesh!"

She immediately searched for his contact and pressed the call button.

After a few rings, the call connected.

"Hello... who's this?" came a familiar voice.

"It's me, Sneha. I need a small favour."

There was a brief pause before Yagnesh chuckled.

"As expected," he teased. "You remember your friends only when you need something."

Sneha couldn't help but smile.

"It's not like that. I'm just not in a situation where I can explain everything right now. Please try to understand."

"Alright, alright," he replied with a laugh. "Relax. Tell me what happened."

Sneha narrated everything—from meeting Siddu on the train to his mysterious disappearance and the strange reservation under Kiran's name.

After listening carefully, Yagnesh said,

"Leave it to me. I'll gather whatever information I can and call you tomorrow morning."

A relieved smile appeared on Sneha's face.

"Thank you so much, Yagnesh."

"Don't mention it," he replied before ending the call.

With nothing more she could do, Sneha leaned against the window.

The rhythmic sound of the train echoed through the night as thoughts of Siddu slowly filled her mind once again.

Somewhere between hope and uncertainty, she quietly drifted off to sleep.

________________________________________

The moon slowly disappeared beyond the horizon, giving way to the first golden rays of morning.

Sneha woke up much earlier than usual.

Every few minutes, her eyes wandered toward her phone, waiting for Yagnesh's call.

Finally, the phone vibrated.

She grabbed it almost instantly.

"Hello!"

"Hello, dear," came a cheerful voice.

Sneha frowned for a second before looking at the screen.

Mom Calling.

She smiled.

"Good morning, Mom."

Her mother laughed.

"Is this really my little princess? I can't believe you've actually woken up this early."

Sneha laughed along.

"Of course it's me. Your little princess has finally learned some responsibility."

Both of them shared a hearty laugh before chatting for a few minutes.

"Alright, Mom," Sneha said. "I'll call you once I reach Delhi. It should take another twelve hours."

"Okay, dear. Take care."

"You too."

After ending the call, Sneha's smile slowly faded.

Her eyes returned to the silent phone.

Why hadn't Yagnesh called yet?

As if answering her thoughts, the phone rang once again.

This time, it was Yagnesh.

Sneha answered immediately.

"Did you find anything?"

"I did," Yagnesh replied. "I managed to gather a few details."

Sneha sat upright.

"The seat Siddu travelled on was booked by his friend Kiran about two weeks ago. But here's the strange part..."

"What?"

"Kiran changed his phone number a week ago. The number you called still exists, but nobody uses it anymore."

Sneha listened carefully.

"There's one more thing," Yagnesh continued.

"Kiran is from Mysuru."

"That's all I could find."

Although it wasn't much, it was the first real clue she had.

"Thank you, Yagnesh. You really helped me."

"Anytime."

The call ended.

Sneha remained silent for a few moments.

Mysuru...

That single word echoed in her mind.

Then another idea crossed her thoughts.

She immediately called her mother.

"Mom... do we have any relatives in Mysuru?"

Her mother answered without hesitation.

"Of course. Your uncle Venkatesh lives there. Don't you remember him?"

Sneha smiled.

"How could I forget? He always treated me like his own daughter."

"Why are you asking?"

"I'll explain later, Mom. I have something important to do."

After ending the call, Sneha immediately dialed her uncle's number.

Following a few warm greetings, she narrated everything that had happened during her journey.

Her uncle listened patiently without interrupting.

When she finished, he spoke reassuringly.

"Don't worry, Sneha. Leave this to me. I'll find Kiran's address and let you know as soon as possible."

Relief washed over her face.

"Thank you, Uncle."

"Take care of yourself first," he replied before ending the call.

Hours passed.

Finally, the train slowed as it entered Delhi Junction.

Sneha picked up her luggage and stood near the door.

Before stepping onto the platform, she looked back at the coach one last time.

Just yesterday, she had boarded this train as an ordinary passenger.

Now she was leaving with countless unanswered questions... and an inexplicable determination to find the stranger who had changed her journey forever.

Taking a deep breath, Sneha stepped onto the platform, unaware that this was only the beginning of a much bigger mystery.
